corrections.form_value: ... while the best human responses matched or exceeded the chatbots' (Table 1; Results, 'Overall human and AI performance').
corrections.source_says: Neither cited location supports the best-human clause. 'Overall human and AI performance' reports AI higher on max scores too (B = 0.027; B = 0.403). The Table 1 Max row puts the top AI session above the top human on both rating scores (3.69 vs 3.56; 4.63 vs 4.25). The clause comes from the Abstract and the Discussion, which compare per-object top scores and name three AI exceptions (Copy.Ai on pencil for max semantic distance; ChatGPT3 and ChatGPT4 on box for max rating). Cite the Abstract and Discussion for that clause.
corrections.quote: Although AI chatbots performed better than humans on average, they did not consistently outperform the best human performers.
corrections.locator: Discussion, paragraph 4; Abstract; Table 1, Max row; Results, per-object subsections (Figs. 4 and 6)

corrections.source_says: The Data availability statement gives one OSF link for the data matrix and the analysis scripts. Both fields should hold https://osf.io/qdz3n/?view_only=d2da32d06f0f4f7ca5bd4bdfc8cf4346. The form records this link only in source.supplement.where.
corrections.quote: The data matrix and analysis scripts are available at OSF.io (https://osf.io/qdz3n/?view_only=d2da32d06f0f4f7ca5bd4bdfc8cf4346).

corrections.form_value: [] in all four contrasts (S1-O1 to S1-O4)
corrections.source_says: For each of the four outcomes the paper prints group N, mean, SD, and 95% CI (Table 1) and a mixed-model B with SE, 95% CI, t(df), and p (Results, 'Overall human and AI performance'). Each list should read ["arm_means_sds_ns", "regression_coefficient_se", "confidence_interval", "test_statistic"]. The AI N counts test sessions, not people (Table 1, note a).
corrections.quote: The semantic distance mean scores (Fig. 2A) and max scores (Fig. 1B) were higher for AI than humans, B = 0.049, SE = 0.010, CI [0.030, 0.069], t(274) = 4.949, p < 0.001
corrections.locator: Results, Table 1; Results, 'Overall human and AI performance', paragraphs 1 and 2

corrections.source_says: S1 analyzed 256 people, and the form-spec counts people analyzed across all arms of the study, so the count criterion is met. Only criterion 1 fails, so core stays "no". The reason should say that the study fails criterion 1 only.
corrections.quote: Of the 279 participants with full data, 256 passed the attention checks (108 females, 145 males, 2 other, and 1 preferred not to identify the gender identity) and their results were included in the present study.
corrections.locator: Method, Participants; form-spec, field note on eligibility.core; codebook section 3

corrections.source_says: Six raters and SemDis semantic distance scored the 256 participants' AUT responses for creativity. Codebook criterion 3 asks only for creativity scored on participants' output by raters or a computed measure, so it is met. The reason's 'no AI-assisted human output to score' describes the criterion 1 failure.
corrections.quote: We collected subjective creativity/originality ratings from six briefly trained humans.

corrections.form_value: shares_participants_with, quote, and locator all empty
corrections.source_says: The human AUT data were collected for another study, whose method was preregistered at https://osf.io/fy3mn/?view_only=f1cf960d0170433dba9d31df68a6eaf7. The paper does not name that study. The form notes the reuse only in participants.who. sample_overlap should record it with this quote and locator.
corrections.quote: The AUT data from human participants were collected in the context of another study and its’ method was preregistered at OSF.io in the context of that study

corrections.source_says: The paper names no primary outcome. It analyzes semantic distance and subjective ratings, mean and max scores, in parallel. Form rule 1 asks for "not_stated" where the form offers it.
corrections.quote: Thus, it is reasonable to analyze the data separately for semantic distance and subjective ratings.
corrections.locator: Results, 'Descriptive statistics and correlations'; Method, 'Statistical analyses'

confirmed: Version: Scientific Reports 13, article 13601, published online 14 September 2023. The XML reads '© The Author(s) 2023, corrected publication 2024' and cites Author Correction 10.1038/s41598-024-54745-y of 20 February 2024 on the Fig. 2D analysis (front matter; back matter, change history; Crossref updated-by). The form's version statement describes what was read and claims no page numbers.

No full text is on file (retrieval.json status not_obtained). I read the Europe PMC full-text XML for PMC10502005 and the Author Correction XML for PMC10879133. The Nature article page returned a bot-check page ('Client Challenge'), and I did not pursue it.
Title and both authors (Mika Koivisto, Simone Grassini) match the document (front matter).

Design class ai_vs_human and context class ai_vs_human are right. 256 Prolific participants did the AUT with no AI, and ChatGPT3.5, ChatGPT4, and Copy.Ai each answered it in 11 sessions. No person received AI help (Method, Participants and Procedure).
No randomized people study. The only randomization is the order in which each rater saw the responses (Method, Scoring). has_randomized_people_study is false.

People counts: 310 opened the link, 279 gave full data, and 256 passed the attention checks and were analyzed. n_randomized null fits, because nobody was assigned to anything. 14 participants lack some object cells (Method, Participants; Method, Scoring).

AI counts: 11 sessions with four objects per chatbot, n = 132 observations (Method, Participants). The Table 1 AI N is 33 test sessions (Table 1, note a). n_units 289 is not printed. It is 256 humans plus 33 sessions, as the notes say, and the paper treats each AI session 'as it were from an individual participant' (Method, Scoring).
participants.quote is verbatim and 36 words long. Age 30.4 (range 19 to 40), 44 students, and countries UK 166, USA 79, Canada 9, and Ireland 2 match (Method, Participants).

All Table 1 values in the four reported strings match cell by cell: means 0.95/0.91, 1.01/0.98, 2.91/2.47, 3.61/3.18; 95% CIs; SDs 0.03/0.06, 0.036/0.053, 0.39/0.47, 0.45/0.53; N 33/256 (Results, Table 1).
Mixed-model strings for S1-O1 to S1-O3 match verbatim: B = 0.049 (t(274) = 4.949), B = 0.027 (t(268) = 3.037, p = 0.003), B = 0.453 (t(282) = 5.496) (Results, 'Overall human and AI performance').

S1-O4 matches the corrected text: B = 0.403, SE = 0.091, CI [0.226, 0.581], t(280) = 4.444, p < 0.001. The Author Correction says the original text had B = 0.453, SE = 0.082 for this analysis (Results, 'Overall human and AI performance'; Author Correction).

The S1-O2 locator Fig. 2B is right: the Fig. 2 caption assigns panels A and B to semantic distance. The paper's text says '(Fig. 1B)', a typo in the source (Results, 'Overall human and AI performance'; Fig. 2 caption).
Direction treatment_higher fits all four pooled AI-versus-human contrasts (Results, 'Overall human and AI performance').

Scoring details match: SemDis mean of five models, multiplicative composition, 'remove filler and clean', and DIY and 'Make a' phrases removed. Six raters, not told about AI, used a 1 to 5 scale and stressed novelty over usefulness. ICCs are 0.88, 0.93, 0.90, and 0.93 (Method, Scoring).

AI tool details match: ChatGPT3 tested 30.3.2023, Copy.Ai 1.4 to 2.4.2023, ChatGPT4 5.4.2023. Ideas per session were fixed (four times 3, twice 2, twice 4, once each 1, 5, and 6), with 1 to 3 words per response (Method, Participants and Procedure).
Task: rope, box, pencil, and candle at 30 s each, with instructions that stress quality over quantity. The about 13-min participation covers the whole session (Method, Participants and Procedure).

Supplement: the paper points to online supplementary material at 10.1038/s41598-023-40858-3 with Supplementary Fig. 1 and analyses that drop the lowest performers (back matter; Method, Procedure; Discussion).
company_involvement false fits: the only funding is University of Bergen open-access funding, and the authors declare no competing interests (back matter).
The one-line finding's numbers match: 0.95 vs 0.91 and 2.91 vs 2.47 (Table 1), and B = 0.453, SE = 0.082 (Results, 'Overall human and AI performance').
Notes: the ChatGPT4-versus-humans contrast on mean ratings, t(283) = -6.6649, is printed (Results, 'Differentiating performance between AI chatbots and objects: human subjective ratings').
summary: The form classifies c077 correctly as ai_vs_human context with no randomized people study (256 Prolific participants without AI against 33 chatbot sessions), and every Table 1 value and mixed-model string, including the corrected Fig. 2D numbers, matches the Europe PMC XML. Seven fields need fixes: the one-line finding cites Table 1 for a best-human claim that only the Abstract and Discussion make, data_and_code, statistics_available, sample_overlap, and primary are empty although the paper supplies them, and criteria 2 and 3 are met as worded while core stays no.
